Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B9.1 (the population-growth passage)

standards.title: Population growth
standards.description: Students model how populations grow and what limits them.
iCan: I can describe exponential growth (a J-shaped curve) as growth without limits, when resources are unlimited
I can describe logistic growth (an S-shaped curve) that levels off at the carrying capacity (K), the most a habitat can sustain
I can explain density-dependent factors (competition, disease, predation) versus density-independent factors (weather, disasters)
I can use a growth graph to identify the growth phase, the carrying capacity, and where growth slows

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q2, Q3; SA 11, 12; Part 3 CER

standards.title: Community ecology
standards.description: Students explain how species interact in a community.
iCan: I can define a community and an ecological niche, and state the competitive exclusion principle
I can describe the interspecific interactions: competition, predation and herbivory, and symbiosis (mutualism, commensalism, parasitism)
I can explain the role of a keystone species (an outsized effect on community structure)
I can describe ecological succession (primary and secondary) as the change in a community over time

standards.title: Ecosystems and energy flow
standards.description: Students trace energy through an ecosystem.
iCan: I can tell apart producers, consumers (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores), and decomposers, and assign trophic levels
I can explain that energy enters as sunlight and flows one way, lost as heat at each step
I can state the roughly 10 percent rule and explain why food chains are short and an energy pyramid narrows upward
I can tell apart energy flow (one-way) from matter (recycled)

exam.examItems: MC Q7, Q8; SA 15; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Biogeochemical cycles
standards.description: Students explain how matter cycles through ecosystems.
iCan: I can explain that, unlike energy, matter is recycled between organisms and the environment
I can describe the carbon cycle: photosynthesis fixes CO2, respiration and combustion release it
I can describe the nitrogen cycle: fixation by bacteria makes nitrogen usable, then it passes through organisms and decomposers
I can describe the water cycle, and explain how burning fossil fuels alters the carbon cycle

standards.title: Biomes, climate, and human impact
standards.description: Students relate biomes to climate and assess human impact.
iCan: I can explain that climate (temperature and precipitation) is the main factor setting terrestrial biomes
I can describe the main aquatic zones briefly and that abiotic factors shape them
I can explain a major human impact accurately: greenhouse-gas driven climate change, habitat loss, or biodiversity decline
I can connect biodiversity to ecosystem stability and name a conservation or restoration strategy
